title: The Interface That Reports Itself: A Harness Through Which Every QML Failure Is Data a Test Can Read

questions.question: A QML handler throws a ReferenceError while a file is loaded through the harness. What does the harness report?
options: A failure of kind warning, with the text of the error
questions.explanation: Seven of the eight cases were a load failure or a warning; this one was a warning.

questions.question: A required property is not given. What kind of failure is it?
questions.explanation: It was a load failure with the text Required property.

questions.question: What does ok() mean?
options: No failure of any kind has been recorded or printed since the last clear
There are no warnings of kind probe
questions.explanation: It is the one question a test asks at the end.

questions.question: A test provokes a warning on purpose. What does it do?
options: Look for that failure by its text, and clear before the next step
questions.explanation: clear forgets, so a test can look at what one step caused.

questions.question: Item { width: 0 / 0 } is loaded. What does the harness say?
options: Nothing: no message was printed or refused, and the width is 0
questions.explanation: It loaded with 0 failures and a width of 0.

questions.question: What does a test have to do about what QML does not say?
options: Ask for it: read the property and assert on its value
questions.explanation: The harness reports what QML says.
